title: Why a $50,000 Car Is Breaking Americans (84-Month Loans)
alts: The 84-Month Car Loan Trick: Lower Payment, Bigger Bill
Car Loans Explained: Why Americans Owe $1.7 Trillion on Cars
line1: Why do new cars cost $50,000 now? And why is a 7-year car loan a trap? Here's how the car deal really works, explained simply.
summary: Dave's old car dies, and the dealer offers him an 84-month loan. We explain why the average new car now costs over $50,000 (chip shortage, trucks and SUVs, vanishing cheap models, tariffs), why a longer auto loan lowers the payment but raises the total interest, how dealer rate markups and add-ons make money in the finance office, depreciation and negative equity rollover, record subprime auto loan delinquencies, and how people buy a car smarter.
